axes.model_access: The server does not call models itself. It is an MCP-facing implementation that wraps Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket and Teamwork Graph search and read/write capabilities as tools for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT and other agents (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: An officially cloud-hosted remote MCP server: one endpoint covers Jira, Confluence and more Atlassian products. The official support page says clients install it into Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT and Claude in one click. The service runs in Atlassian’s cloud, not as a local process (2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: No local filesystem access. The scope is issue, page, Bitbucket repository and project metadata on the Atlassian cloud site. The client keeps only connection configuration and tool-call records, with no site content cached locally (2026-11-21).
axes.background: MCP tool calls execute with the client request, and the service runs on Atlassian’s side. There is no independent job queue or delayed work. Long operations are governed by the client’s own timeouts and retries (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: The official product page lists Jira issue search/create and Confluence page search/create, plus Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT and Claude clients. The support page adds Rovo search/fetch, Teamwork Graph context and audit logging. The full tool list should be checked against the official docs and the client’s tool list (2026-11-21).
axes.context: There is no server-side cross-session memory. Each tool call reads data under the current OAuth 2.1 grant and site state. State lives in Jira/Confluence, not in conversation context retained by the MCP server (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: OAuth 2.1 user authorisation: what the agent can see equals the connected account’s site permissions, including project-level limits. Official docs say site or org admins can manage, review or revoke the MCP app’s access. They also list domain and IP allowlists and an audit-log event for every tool call. Write capabilities take effect directly, so assume it can edit your wiki (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: enterprise development flows where an agent needs Jira requirement context, writes Confluence docs and searches across Bitbucket and Teamwork Graph. Not fit: approval workflows. Data Center self-hosted support should follow the official docs (2026-11-21).

mcp.transport:
**Streamable HTTP remote hosting** (official endpoint); verified: product page 200 (2026-10-21).
The concrete endpoint URL follows the official docs (not verified item by item).
mcp.auth: OAuth 3LO (user login authorization); scopes are split by product (separate scope families for Jira / Confluence).
mcp.scope:
Read surface: issue/page search and reading; write surface: create/update issues, create/update pages.
It follows the account's permissions; there is no tool-level approval layer.

runs: This entry checks the official product page, support page and developer guide. Tool calls, write operations and project-level permissions need item-by-item validation on a test site.
